item.title: Localizing an Interface
item.description: Follow the team behind a fictional equipment reservation portal as they translate interface text, check regional formats, and test how the translations appear.

children.definition: A point in the development schedule after which the original interface text is kept stable so translators can finish their work.
children.example: The team scheduled a string freeze for Friday so translators could finish the portal’s interface text without having to redo translations after source edits.
children.translation_uz: interfeysning asl matniga oʻzgartirish kiritish toʻxtatiladigan bosqich

children.definition: A marker embedded in a piece of interface text that the software substitutes with a value when it displays the text.
children.example: In “Collect from {location}”, the translator moved the placeholder to the beginning because the pickup location needed to come first in the translated instruction.

children.definition: A software setting that identifies a language and, where relevant, a region, so the interface can apply the appropriate linguistic and formatting conventions.
children.example: The tester switched the portal to the UK English locale and checked that the collection date appeared with the day before the month.

children.definition: Text from another language or regional variant that the software displays when the requested version is missing.
children.example: When a help string is missing in Canadian French, the portal displays the French (France) version as a fallback translation.

children.definition: The increase in length that occurs when a translation needs more space than the original wording.
children.example: The designer allowed for text expansion in the reservation buttons because the German action phrases were longer than the English ones.

children.definition: A word or expression recorded in a project’s vocabulary list with its intended meaning or preferred translation.
children.example: The linguist added ‘collection point’ as a glossary term and specified that it meant the counter where users pick up reserved equipment.

children.definition: An instruction or explanation attached to a piece of interface text to help the person rendering it in another language.
children.example: The writer added a translator note explaining that ‘Hold’ was an action that temporarily reserved equipment.

children.definition: A view that shows translated wording in its intended position within the interface before users see it.
children.example: The in-context preview showed that ‘Reserve’ appeared on a button beneath the equipment details, so the linguist chose a verb in the translation.
children.translation_uz: tarjimaning interfeysda qanday koʻrinishini oldindan koʻrish

children.definition: A language-specific convention that determines which grammatical form a phrase takes for a given quantity.
children.example: The Polish plural rule made the portal display ‘2 urządzenia’ for two devices and ‘5 urządzeń’ for five.
children.translation_ru: правило выбора грамматической формы в зависимости от количества
children.translation_uz: songa qarab grammatik shaklni tanlash qoidasi

children.definition: The practice of using the same agreed expression for a given concept wherever it occurs in a product.
children.example: To maintain terminology consistency, the linguist used the same translation of ‘reservation’ in the confirmation and on the cancellation button.

children.definition: The loss of part of the displayed text when the interface cuts it off to fit the space provided.
children.example: On the narrow layout, truncation hid the word ‘tomorrow’ at the end of the translated pickup reminder.

children.definition: A convention for presenting a calendar day, including the sequence of its components and how they are written or separated.
children.example: To check the UK date format, the tester entered 6 April and confirmed that the portal displayed it as 06/04, with the day before the month.

children.definition: Adapted to the conventions associated with a particular language or regional variant.
children.example: The portal uses locale-specific number formatting to display the deposit as 25.50 in UK English and 25,50 in French.
children.translation_uz: muayyan til yoki hudud meʼyorlariga mos

children.definition: Language that presents a situation without assigning blame or expressing judgement.
children.example: The linguist chose neutral wording for the failed extension and wrote ‘This reservation could not be extended’ in the portal.
collocations: use neutral wording in an error prompt
